title: Pre-registered source-split test on c11's ringed rods fails narrowly: the rod-made share of the surfactant forms a layer at rim/core 1.46-1.51 with 53-59% of individuals passing (bar: 2/3), and 1.37 at 1.5x, so B stays by construction; S, I, M, D replicate on fresh seed 9
summary: Ran c00's pre-registered experiment for Q:nematic-ring-made-by-rods: world_srcsplit3.py (c11's world with three passive copies of the surfactant, made on rod, interface and far-bath pixels; bodies unchanged because s does not act back) with labkit on seeds 0, 1, 2 and fresh seed 9, at 1.5x (dx 0.6667, 192^2, seed 0, T=600), and a chis=0 twin on seed 2. By signed distance to the phi=0 contour the rod-made copy has aggregate rim/core 1.49/1.46/1.51/1.50 and rim/out 4.8-5.1, with 57/53/59/54% of individual body-frames passing both ratios (sd_individuals.py), against 2.2 for the interface- and bath-made copies; at 1.5x it falls to 1.37 (16% of 55 body-frames; few bodies nucleate there), and chis=0 gives a diffuse fill (0.72). The ring's material is 37% rod-made, 24% interface-made, 39% far-bath-made. The pass rule (>= 2/3 of individuals on 3/3 seeds and at 1.5x) fails, so B is by construction for this line, as the question's fail branch states. The rods themselves replicate: from noise, 13-23 persistent splits (generation 3-4) and up to 3.5-5.7 body lengths of travel on seeds 0, 1, 2 and 9.

verdicts.track_note: I did not re-trace the claim's track 46 of seed 2 in the rod-made channel alone; the per-individual test covers every body-frame

controls_run.B: split/, split2/, fresh9/ (source split), chis0/ (rod-only drift off: diffuse fill), res15/ (1.5x); results.txt

verdicts.limitation: The fail is narrow: the rod-made copy sits at the 1.5 bar in aggregate (1.46-1.51) and passes in about 55% of individuals, so a slightly stronger drift or rod source could push it over; at 1.5x few bodies nucleate with the registered noise, so that arm is weak. In the fuel-cell variant a rod-only ring also forms but stays far below its gate (my audit 20261025T2005), consistent with this. Distances are in pixels, not rescaled at 1.5x.
